data.question_intent: Clarification on rate sensitivity and hedge income impact, and updates on methodology, policy changes, and operational risk (OR1) figures.
data.question_quote: the piece that I'm still struggling with a bit is the rate sensitivity, the £50m in year-one, I hear what you're saying about a lot of that being relating to deposit lag, but if there's £40bn of hedge maturities a year as per guidance, you'd have thought a 25 basis point shift in the curve would be knocking £50m out of the hedge income in year one.
data.answer_quote: So we said £170bn over three years. So I think you're probably closer to around £60bn of hedge maturing.
data.reason: The answer directly addresses the rate sensitivity question with a high level of evidence, providing a specific figure for hedge maturities and explaining the impact of rate changes on hedge income. It also responds to the second question with a direct answer, although it defers the operational risk (OR1) figures to a follow-up discussion.
